newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends down on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends down on profit-taking.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended slightly down in slow trade on Friday on profit-taking from retail investors, traders said.
The most actively traded October 1997 contract ended at an intraday low of 23,390 yuan ($2,821) per tonne, losing 60 yuan. It opened at 23,400 and hit a high of 23,490.
July lost 20 yuan to 22,780, August 50 to 22,970, September 60 to 23,170, November 10 to 23,510 and December 20 to 23,530.
Combined volume fell to 20,210 tonnes from 38,760.
Copper opened little changed from Thursday's close and fell steadily for most of the session.
Traders said many investors stayed on the sidelines today due to the recent consolidation on the London Metal Exchange and a lack of domestic market-moving news.
"Only speculative players for quick profits took part in today's trading and most investors were reluctant to trade ahead of the weekend," one trader said.
"Weak physical prices also encumbered the futures prices," he said.
Physical prices are around 22,750/800 yuan today due to weak demand, traders said.
They said copper would linger around current levels early next week due to weak market sentiment.
"Copper is likely to move in a range of 23,200 and 23,800 yuan in the short term waiting for fresh stimulus," a second trader said.
Aluminium ended little changed. July did not trade, August was unchanged at 14,300 and September fell 80 yuan to 14,500.
Combined volume fell to 450 tonnes from 950.
